aspect: Export control is not a hiring rule
description: DOJ's position: the ITAR and the EAR contain no employment or hiring requirements and do not require employers or staffing agencies to limit jobs to US citizens. If a foreign person's job needs access to controlled technical data, the employer obtains a licence for that person.
energy_note: The reason you were given does not exist in the regulation.

aspect: The definition that employers get wrong
description: ITAR 120.62 defines 'US person' to include lawful permanent residents under 8 USC 1101(a)(20) AND 'protected individuals' under 8 USC 1324b(a)(3) - which covers asylees and refugees. Restricting an export-controlled role to citizens and green card holders unlawfully excludes asylees and refugees.
energy_note: Three categories of lawful worker, excluded by a definition nobody read.

aspect: EXAMPLE - Clifford Chance US LLP, 2018, USD 132,000
description: DOJ found the firm unlawfully restricted staffing by citizenship status, excluding non-US citizens AND DUAL US CITIZENS from document review involving ITAR-controlled data. DOJ attributed it to a misunderstanding of ITAR. Civil penalty: USD 132,000.
energy_note: Dual citizens excluded - which is every Iranian-American, because Iran will not let the nationality go.
source_name: DOJ IER settlements via National Law Review
notes: The dual-citizen element connects directly to STA-002: Iranians cannot renounce, so this exclusion lands on them permanently.

description: DOJ found at least 25 job postings requiring applicants to be 'lawful permanent residents and/or US citizens' without valid justification, again from a misunderstanding of ITAR/EAR. Penalty USD 44,626 plus two years of DOJ monitoring.

aspect: EXAMPLE - American CyberSystems, and General Motors
description: DOJ concluded there was no justification for excluding US nationals, asylees and refugees from a posting, because no authorisation was needed to share controlled items with them. Separately DOJ determined GM's method of running export compliance assessments discriminated against non-US workers, and issued an employer fact sheet alongside the settlement.

aspect: The exact postings that are unlawful
description: DOJ names them: 'Only U.S. Citizens', 'Only U.S. Citizens or Green Card Holders', or demanding a US birth certificate - even where the role genuinely requires authorisation. The recommended wording is 'U.S. person'.
energy_note: If you have seen those words on a posting, you have seen a violation.

aspect: Do not merge the export check with the I-9
description: DOJ advises against combining an export compliance assessment with the Form I-9 process - a common practice that turns a document check into a citizenship screen.

aspect: Settlements are rising, and they are small
description: IER reaches dozens of settlements annually, with a small but increasing share tied to EAR/ITAR/DOE compliance. The penalties - USD 44,626, USD 132,000 - are rounding errors for the companies involved, which is why the practice persists.
energy_note: A remedy that exists, works, and costs the employer less than complying would have.

aspect: SCENARIO - the posting he screenshots and does nothing about
description: Omid finds a role he is qualified for. The posting says 'Must be a U.S. Citizen or Green Card Holder'. He is an asylee, which makes him a protected individual and a US person. He screenshots it, looks up how to file with IER, reads that it takes months, and applies somewhere else.
energy_note: Holding a valid legal claim and no time to use it.
